mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates broad-based demand weakness that triggers reduced corporate revenue expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 110, supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output signal potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 110, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past three months indicates strong demand for goods and services, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when RSAFS increases, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 210 in a month, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 210, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or interaction Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), policy rate hikes reduce liquidity and increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over the last 5 years.
